entry_thesis: New Zealand's 10-year cash yield is 4.98 percent against the US 10-year at 5.21 percent, so NZ minus US 10-year sits at minus 23 basis points, the first percentile of one-year history and the 0.3rd percentile of five-year history, after a 30 basis-point one-month cheapening in which the US 10-year rose 25 basis points and New Zealand's 10-year fell only 3. That is a cash peer-duration dislocation, not a 2-year pack because the kiwi is cheap: cash NZ minus US 2-year is already minus 99 basis points, and kiwi at 0.5613 is a separate spot residual. Convergence is pay New Zealand 10-year versus receive US 10-year so the spread rises toward its historical New Zealand premium; the 13 January 2025…
